messages.subject: Re: Previous NBLAST Documentation
parts:
Dear LauraAnn, 

glad to hear that nblast is proving useful. However I can think of no reason to expect a change in results based on differences in the package code. In particular the nhclust clustering function continues to use the same implementation of Ward’s method as the default. If you do want to roll back the package to a previous version, google “MRAN” then use that to install. In terms of a possible source of differences, are you sure you are preparing the dotprops version of neurons in the same way? We often add two arguments 

resample=1, k=5 

to the dotprops call, which will have effects on the calculated scores.

All the best, Greg. 

PS if you are interested in reproducible research in R, there are quite a lot of resources. In general the key things are to version control your own code, use rmarkdown files to isolate your analysis in single files with all steps. You can also use the renv package to specify versions of all your dependencies. Finally you may be interested in a Docker image that we have been working on recently, which provides a complete environment including rstudio. https://hub.docker.com/r/natverse/r-natverse

Sent from my iPhone

On 21 May 2020, at 22:05, LauraAnn Schmidberger <lauraann.s...@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿
Hello Dr. Jefferis,

I hope you are doing well!

Last year I ran NBLAST on a set of zebrafish neurons. I assume I was using 1.6.2, since that was the last released version and I was not using the dev version. Recently I repeated my code with the same set of neurons (using the version released in January, 1.6.5) and saw slightly different clustering. I was unable to find complete documentation for the previous version, so I thought I would ask you. I know that the clustering method was and still is ward, but were there any changes to the scoring methods etc? I do not have my own scoring matrix and I have never specified a sigma etc...
For reference, here is my very simple code:

>new_neurons=read.neurons(“path/folder”)

>new_neurons.dps=dotprops(new_neurons)

>abascores=nblast_allbyall(new_neurons.dps)

>aba.hclust=nhclust(scoremat=abascores)


(And then I plot the dendrogram into a .jpg or .svg)


Thank you in advance for any insight!


Best,

LauraAnn Schmidberger
